nodes.label: yt-dlp simulate-mode URL resolution (-g / -j)
nodes.summary: The invocation contract for resolving an audio-only stream URL without downloading: `yt-dlp -f "bestaudio[ext=m4a]/bestaudio" -g --no-playlist <URL>`. `-g, --get-url` is documented as an alias for `--print urls`; `--print` implies `--quiet` and `--simulate` unless `--no-simulate`, so nothing is written to disk. `-x, --extract-audio` hard-requires ffmpeg and ffprobe, but is unnecessary for pure playback: `-g -f bestaudio` returns the original webm/opus or m4a/aac stream untranscoded. `ba*`/`bestaudio*` means 'may also contain video' and upstream says do not use it. For an app, `-j`/`-J` is better than `-g` because the same simulate semantics also yield `%(ext)s`, `%(acodec)s`, `%(availability)s` and `%(playable_in_embed)s`.

nodes.label: googlevideo URL expiry, IP binding and signature
nodes.norm_label: googlevideo url expiry, ip binding and signature
nodes.summary: A resolved googlevideo media URL is time-limited, IP-bound and signed on three axes, which the note calls the biggest architectural constraint of the whole path. A real URL pasted in yt-dlp issue #14936 contains `expire=<unix ts>`, `ip=<client IP>`, `sparams=expire,ei,ip,id,itag,...`, `lsig=` and `sig=`, and returns HTTP 403 when replayed (closed as not_planned by maintainer bashonly). The official FAQ states that in many cases requests for the video must come from the same IP address and with the same cookies and/or HTTP headers. The commonly quoted 6 h TTL is derived, not documented: in #14936 `expire - met` = 1762604258 - 1762582658 = exactly 21600 s, but yt-dlp never parses `expire` and YouTube publishes no TTL, so it is medium confidence and must not be treated as a contract.

nodes.label: googlevideo HTTP header requirements: User-Agent yes, Referer no
nodes.norm_label: googlevideo http header requirements: user-agent yes, referer no
nodes.summary: For a `*.googlevideo.com/videoplayback` request, a browser-like User-Agent is always sent and Referer is neither sent nor required. `std_headers` contains `User-Agent` from `random_user_agent()` (a Chrome 145-151 string on Windows), plus Accept, Accept-Language and Sec-Fetch-Mode, and no Referer; the YouTube extractor sets no per-format `http_headers` for media formats (the only `http_headers` read in `_video.py` is for the PO-token request). Cookies are needed only for private, age-restricted or members-only content. The note is explicit that the realistic 403 cause is not a header at all: it is IP binding, `n`-challenge throttling, or a missing GVS PO Token, where `_report_pot_format_skipped` states skipped formats 'require a GVS PO Token which was not provided. They will be skipped as they may yield HTTP Error 403.'

nodes.label: HTTP Range support on googlevideo URLs
nodes.norm_label: http range support on googlevideo urls
nodes.summary: Range requests work against the direct googlevideo URL, which is what makes seeking possible. yt-dlp's native HTTP downloader sets `request.headers['Range'] = f'bytes={start}-{end}'`, validates the response `Content-Range` header to decide whether resume is possible, retries without the header on `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable`, and carries a YouTube-specific special case: 'in issue #175 it was revealed that YouTube sometimes adds or removes a few bytes from the end of the file'. The YouTube extractor separately relies on a server-side `range` query parameter for fragmented formats. Player-side constraint: the FAQ states 'YouTube throttles any request with an http chunk size of > 10MB', so range windows must stay at or below 10 MB.

nodes.label: yt-dlp-ejs JavaScript runtime requirement
nodes.summary: A JavaScript runtime is now required for full YouTube support: the README lists `yt-dlp-ejs` as 'Required for full YouTube support' and deno, node.js, bun or QuickJS as the runtimes that execute it. Versions: Deno >= 2.3.0 (recommended, enabled by default), Node >= 22.0.0 via `--js-runtimes node`, QuickJS >= 2023-12-9, Bun 1.2.11-1.3.14 only with support deprecated; priority deno > node > quickjs > bun. Absence of a runtime fails silently rather than loudly: 'If no JavaScript runtime/engine is available, then `web` is omitted', from `_DEFAULT_CLIENTS = ('visionos', 'web')` against `_DEFAULT_JSLESS_CLIENTS = ('visionos',)`, and `if skip_player_js: continue` drops any format whose URL still carries an `n` challenge.

nodes.label: yt-dlp player_client selection and PO Token policy
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp player_client selection and po token policy
nodes.summary: Available clients are `web`, `web_safari`, `web_embedded`, `web_music`, `web_creator`, `mweb`, `ios`, `visionos`, `android`, `android_vr`, `tv`, `tv_downgraded`, `tv_simply`, and the default is `visionos,web`. The pinned Known Issues recommend overriding that default: for 'web only has SABR formats' (#12482) the guidance is to try PO Tokens with the `mweb` or `web_creator` client, and the Extractors wiki says to use `mweb` with a PO Token when the defaults misbehave. YouTube is gradually enforcing PO Tokens and yt-dlp cannot generate them - they must be supplied externally, so a PO Token provider plugin or `bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider` is the supported path. The per-client policy table in source marks `web` on HTTPS/DASH as `required=True` and `visionos` as needing none. Other pinned advice: `--force-ipv4` for immediate 403s (#11868) and `-S proto:https` to avoid the iOS HLS seek bug (#9552).

nodes.label: yt-dlp standalone binary vendoring on Linux
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp standalone binary vendoring on linux
nodes.summary: yt-dlp can be shipped inside an app rather than required from the user. Arch's official repository carries `yt-dlp 2026.08.19-1` at architecture `any` with `yt-dlp-ejs` as a hard dependency and ffmpeg only optional, so a pacman install gets EJS support out of the box but is driven by the system interpreter - vendoring that build means shipping Python too. Upstream release files offer `yt-dlp` (platform-independent zipimport, needs Python, recommended for Linux/BSD) and `yt-dlp_linux` (glibc 2.17+ standalone x86_64 binary), plus musllinux and aarch64 builds; `yt-dlp-ejs` is bundled in both the PyInstaller binaries and the official zipimport Unix binary. Even so the JS runtime stays external - Deno is still needed alongside `yt-dlp_linux`. Update channels are `stable` (default, often stale and prone to external breakage), `nightly` (the recommended channel for regular users) and `master`; a vendored copy must be updated by the app's own updater because the stable binary refuses to auto-jump channels.

nodes.label: yt-dlp PyInstaller GPLv3+ licensing trap for vendoring
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp pyinstaller gplv3+ licensing trap for vendoring
nodes.summary: A licensing trap that decides which build may be vendored: 'The PyInstaller-bundled executables include GPLv3+ licensed code, and as such the combined work is licensed under GPLv3+.' Only 'the git repository, the PyPI source distribution and the PyPI built distribution (wheel) only contain code licensed under the Unlicense', while the zipimport `yt-dlp` and `yt-dlp.tar.gz` are ISC/MIT. The note's practical verdict for a Tauri app is to ship a vendored `yt-dlp_linux` (self-contained, EJS bundled, no Python needed) while accepting the GPLv3+ obligation, or avoiding it by shipping the wheel/zipimport build instead, and either vendoring Deno or declaring and detecting the runtime dependency rather than requiring a user-installed yt-dlp.

nodes.label: yt-dlp exit-code and stderr error contract
nodes.norm_label: yt-dlp exit-code and stderr error contract
nodes.summary: The complete set of exit codes, per maintainer pukkandan: 0 success, 100 yt-dlp must restart for update to complete, 101 download cancelled by --max-downloads and similar, 2 error in user-provided options, 1 any other error. Confirmed against current source: `_exit(1)` for CookieLoadError/DownloadError/UnsafeExecExpansionError, `_exit(2, ...)` for optparse errors, `_download_retcode = 100` on updater exception, `return 101` on DownloadCancelled. There is no per-error-class exit code and no `error` key in the JSON info dict, so mapping to user-facing messages must be done on stderr text, whose format is `ERROR: ` + `[ie_key ]` + `video_id: ` + `orig_msg` + optional `(caused by ...)`, with a bug-report blurb appended for unexpected errors only (`expected=True` suppresses it). Concrete classes: `Video unavailable`; 'Playback on other websites has been disabled by the video owner (web_embedded player response playability status: UNPLAYABLE)' as the closest analogue to YouTube IFrame error 153 and a high-priority pinned known issue (#17497); private detected from badge `PRIVACY_PRIVATE` / `videoDetails.isPrivate` and surfaced as `availability`; age gate matched on substrings 'confirm your age', 'age-restricted', 'age_verification_required'; bot check as error #10128, intractable, guidance being a different IP or a PO Token provider; rate limit `This content isn't available, try again later.` (#11426) capped near 300 videos/hour for guest sessions; blocked IP as `All player responses are invalid. Your IP is likely being blocked by Youtube`. `--ignore-errors`/`-i` makes the exit code unreliable for batch use, so prefer one invocation per video, and `--newline`/`--no-progress` are needed when capturing stderr because progress uses `\r`.
